title: [native_aot][5/7] gen_aot_lib: emitted CMake, the version script, generation ordering
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #191669
* #190899
* #190898
* #190897
* #194243
* #194242
* __->__ #194241
* #194240
* #194239
* #194238
* #190896

Human note:

Driver script for generation -- controls how the previous commits are put together
into one cohesive thing. Generates the cmake for libtorch_cuda relinking.

Claude note:

The generator gains a driver, and with it the build integration the previous
commit left out.

native_aot.cmake is not data for CMake to parse -- it IS the CMake calls, so
caffe2/CMakeLists.txt is a single include(... OPTIONAL). An earlier version put
~370 lines of parsing and comparison in CMake, none of it reachable by a test. The
link options are emitted in one exact spelling because each part is load-bearing:
target_link_options de-duplicates, so bare -Xlinker tokens collapse and the link
fails; LINKER: expands to -Wl, which the driver splits on commas; SHELL: splits its
own value on spaces.

Ordering is the correctness argument. The old file is deleted first, sources are
buffered until every declaration has passed its refusals, and the new file is
written atomically and last, so its CONTENT is the only evidence a generation
finished. export.py joins that rule here, invalidating the previous generation
before touching an artifact and on every refusal -- artifacts are direct link
inputs in build.ninja, so an interrupted export plus an ordinary `cmake --build`
relinked a library mixing two source revisions. Invalidation OVERWRITES the
include with its nothing-to-embed form rather than deleting it: CMake registers an
include()d file as a configure dependency only if it existed at configure time, so
a deleted one made the next generation invisible to `cmake --build` and the
kernels stayed out of the library however many times it was rebuilt.

The version script localizes the objects' _mlir_* entry points, which export_to_c
gives default visibility and which would otherwise join torch_cuda's public ABI. A
static torch_cuda cannot take it at all, because CMake silently discards
target_link_options for an archive -- the script would evaporate while appearing to
be applied -- so the verdict in the next commit refuses such a build outright.

Test Plan:

```
pytest tools/test/test_native_aot_tools.py
```

Run at this commit's own tree, in a checkout with no built torch -- which is
what lint.yml's "Test tools" job has. This commit's tests cover the emitted
CMake calls and the opt-out among them, every version-script pattern being
anchored on a kernel prefix and the `local:` directive itself, the delete-first /
buffer-sources / write-last ordering and the atomic write, invalidation leaving an
include a later generation is still seen through, generation scoped to this
build's arch list, and the sidecar-field and orphan-artifact refusals.

Authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).

items.author: albanD
items.body: This sounds like a very specific failure
items.diff_hunk:
@@ -568,3 +578,641 @@ def covers_signature(op: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
         ", ".join(params),
         f"covers_{decl.decl_id_for_op(op)}({schema_args}) -> bool",
     )
+
+
+VERSION_SCRIPT = "native_aot_local.ver"
+
+VER_TMPL = """\
+/* @generated by tools/native_aot/gen_aot_lib.py -- do not edit
+ *
+ * Localize the exported kernel objects' entry points. export_to_c gives them
+ * default visibility and they link straight into torch_cuda, so without this
+ * they would join its public ABI: hundreds of names with no stability
+ * guarantee, tied to the DSL's codegen. The generated launchers are the only
+ * callers and share the link, so localizing costs nothing.
+ *
+ * Generated so every pattern is anchored on a kernel prefix: a bare
+ * `*_cuda_init` would also localize unrelated extern "C" symbols, and a symbol
+ * silently leaving the ABI is painful to debug. `local:` alone restricts
+ * nothing else -- with no `global:` the linker still exports everything else.
+ */
+{{
+  local:
+{patterns}
+}};
+"""
+
+
+def surviving_sidecars(op: str, sidecars: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
+    """The sidecars generation will actually wire a launcher up to.
+
+    _by_arch's tie-break drops candidates, and EVERY consumer must agree on the
+    surviving set: the launchers, the linked objects, the version script and the
+    reported count. Computed privately inside gen_op, it left main() building the
+    other three from the UNFILTERED list, and the dropped objects shipped insi [truncated]
